name: Mascot
lede: Mascot is a very dark navy blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, and the reason for its name is undocumented.

sections.title: A name from a color dictionary
sections.body:
Mascot appears in our library from one source only, Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color*, which gives 1892 as its first recorded year and places it on plate 40 [1]. Neighbors on the same plate include Musketeer, dated 1920, and Romany, dated 1928 [1]. Mascot and Romany carry the same plate address, 40 E 12, in our data, which we cannot explain [1].

Why the color is called Mascot is unrecorded in the books we hold [2]. The word appears once in their text, in a passage about the acid-yellow smiley, called an informal mascot of rave culture [2]. It has nothing to do with this color.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The nearest named colors are [[navy]], [[midnight-blue]] and [[indigo]], and [[slate]] is also close [1]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 133 (0.56 per cent) hold a color within six units over at least five per cent of the canvas [3]. The 1900s hold 27 of them, 2.9 times the archive rate [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [3].

questions.q: Which dictionary is the only source for Mascot in our library?
True or false: the books explain that Mascot was named for a team mascot.

openers: Mascot the color has no recorded origin; the one book mention of the word is about a smiley face.
